name: Ofo
confidence_why: Nothing read states where Ofo stress falls: Rankin's 2004 handout says only that any vowel may be accented or unaccented, Swanton 1909 and Dorsey and Swanton 1912 mark accent in varying positions with one hedged near-minimal pair (i'ya 'deer' vs iya' 'raccoon'), Martin 2001 and Voegelin 1939 are silent, and Rankin's 2024 grammar sketch, the fullest description, has not been read.

catalog_quote: All vowels except ə may occur either long or short, and all vowels without exception may occur accented or unaccented.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on the rendered page image of the held Rankin 2004 handout, p.2 lines 1-2, locator exact. (2) The deciding source is a 12-page 2004 conference handout; its sentence is about vowel distribution, so not determinable is a fair reading of what we hold, and the held primaries (Swanton 1909, Dorsey & Swanton 1912, Rankin-Carter-Jones) add no placement statement -- only observational variation in headword accent position and one hedged near-minimal pair (i'ya 'deer' vs iya' 'raccoon'). (3) But the language's principal description, Rankin 2024 'An Ofo Grammar Sketch' (66 pp, Brill; plus the 2015 published chapter), exists and has not been read by anyone in our reading (paywalled; WAF-blocked 9/12 and again today; not OA per Crossref/OAPEN/DOAB). An absence-of-statement classification is exactly what a full sketch by the same author is likely to overturn (most plausibly to LEXIC
audit.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: re-rendered p.2 of the held Rankin 2004 LAVIS III handout, page renders, image read): lines 1-2 are verbatim 'All vowels except ə may occur either long or short, and all vowels without exception may occur accented or unaccented.' -- locator exact; the text layer's only accent/stress/syllable hit in all 12 pp is this line (a full-text search for stress/accent). It is a distributional statement, not a placement or predictability statement, so not determinable is a fair reading of what is.
